qt: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D), Yannis Maniatis (S&D), Nikos Papandreou (S&D), Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D) Subject:

The International Energy Agency estimates that the electricity consumption of data centres in Europe will increase by around 70 % between 2024 and 20301. On 21 September 2026, the Commission proposed a common rating system for data centres, with an A to G rating for energy and water efficiency, and launched the consultation process on minimum performance standards2. At the same time, however, energy class and efficiency data collected under Directive (EU) 2023/17913 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/13644 are only published on an aggregated basis, at Member State and EU level. However, it remains crucial that the costs of developing and strengthening the electricity grids serving data centres are fairly distributed and not passed on to other consumers. In view of this, can the Commission say: 1.

In order to enhance transparency, will power, energy and water consumption, and the PUE, WUE, ERF and REF metrics be published for each data centre facility, whilst ensuring that only genuinely sensitive information is protected?
How is it ensured that the cost of strengthening electricity grids for data centres is fairly borne by investors and not passed on to consumers?

Will it include, in its forthcoming proposal on minimum performance standards, specific provisions on water consumption for areas facing water stress (a shortage of both drinking and irrigation water) and provide for specific measures for periods of drought?
